memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The territory of Manasseh extended from Asher to Mikmethath east of Shechem. The boundary ran southward from there to include the people living at En Tappuah. (Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but Tappuah itself, on the boundary of Manasseh, belonged to the Ephraimites.) Then the boundary continued south to the Kanah Ravine. There were towns belonging to Ephraim lying among the towns of Manasseh, but the boundary of Manasseh was the northern side of the ravine and ended at the Mediterranean Sea - Josh 17:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The borders of Manasseh are traced, and once again we see the tribes' lands interwoven — towns of Ephraim lying among the towns of Manasseh, with shared boundaries and overlapping territory. The two Joseph tribes lived side by side, their inheritances knit together rather than sharply divided. Family land bordered family land.

We noticed this weaving of tribes earlier, and Scripture returns to it because it matters. God's people were not meant to live in isolation, each fenced off in a private plot. Their lives touched, overlapped, and depended on one another. The borders were shared, and so, inevitably, was daily life. Brothers dwelt near brothers.

This remains God's design for His people. We are not called to a solitary faith but to a shared life, our days interwoven with the lives of other believers. The New Testament calls us one body, deeply connected, unable to say to one another, "I don't need you" (1 Cor 12:21). Like Ephraim and Manasseh, our portions overlap; we are meant to live near enough to one another to share burdens, encourage, and belong. A faith lived entirely alone was never God's intention. We flourish, as these tribes did, side by side.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is your faith lived in isolation, or woven together with other believers?
- How might God be calling you to live nearer to His people, sharing life?
- What does it mean to truly belong to the one body of Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You knit Your people's lives together. Draw me out of isolation and into the shared life of Your family, that I may belong, support, and be supported. Amen.
